clue.text: Lawn weed? Cut the whole lot up

parts.note: to prune is to cut back

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the whole lot is all of it

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to chop up every last weed in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunella, or self-heal, is a low plant that commonly invades lawns; the question mark admits it is one weed among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella vulgaris, self-heal, is a creeping wildflower that gardeners treat as a lawn weed, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Bulb — its brightness?

parts.note: surface reading: a plant bulb, or a bulb rated for how bright it is
setter's reading: a light bulb together with the light it gives, i.e. the whole light fitting

explanation.surface: Someone asks how bright a particular bulb is.
explanation.walkthrough: In lighting trade usage a bulb is itself called a lamp, and the source of its brightness is what the answer names; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device that gives out light, and electricians use the word for the bulb itself, so it covers both bulb and brightness.

clue.text: Vengeful trio that is wearing winter outfits

indicators.note: something being worn sits inside the clothing, so these letters go within the outfits

parts.note: furs are warm winter coats
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Three avengers are pictured dressed for cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Furies were three goddesses of vengeance pursuing wrongdoers.

clue.text: Originally named 'Beds' — to change is necessary

indicators.note: letters told to change get moved into a new order

parts.note: née marks a woman's original surname, literally 'born'
the four letters of Beds rearranged

explanation.surface: A rename from 'Beds' is being justified as unavoidable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally named' looks like it wants a first letter; it is the word née, used before a maiden name. Beds is also the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'if needs be' means 'if it is required', so the expression stands for something being unavoidable.

clue.text: Middle East and Sicily somehow give rise to unfriendly grin

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated arrangement

parts.note: ME is the standard abbreviation for the Middle East
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mediterranean politics seems to produce a frosty smile from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy smile is a cold, hostile one, the opposite of a warm and friendly expression.

clue.text: Horribly wrong, like certain Satie compositions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a plan that has failed badly
second meaning: Erik Satie wrote Trois morceaux en forme de poire, three pieces in the form of a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: To 'go pear-shaped' is British slang for going badly wrong. Satie's piano duet title translates as Three Pieces in the Shape of a Pear.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is both the idiom for a failed venture and a literal description of the shape Satie named his pieces after.

clue.text: One of the Kardashians upset over a party for emperor

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down entry that flips the name to read upwards

parts.note: Kim Kardashian is the best known of the reality-TV family
taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Kardashian is annoyed about a party thrown in someone's honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the turned name above the rest in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado was the title used by foreigners for the Emperor of Japan, as in the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.

clue.text: Animal's awfully cute rear

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters end up in a messed-up order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admires a pet's extremely sweet backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal's' reads as possessive but is 'Animal is', joining definition to wordplay; 'awfully' pretends to intensify 'cute'.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living being, especially an animal as distinct from a person.

clue.text: To obtain acknowledgement, order direct

indicators.note: to order things is to put them into a fresh sequence

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to buy straight from the supplier if you want recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order direct' sounds like shopping advice; 'order' is a verb meaning rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is public recognition given for a contribution, as in film credits.

clue.text: Have a break! Have a ginger biscuit!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ginger ... is a crisp ginger biscuit

explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the KitKat slogan 'Have a break, have a KitKat', swapping in a different biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap means a sudden break as a noun, and a gingersnap is a brittle spiced biscuit, often just called a snap.

clue.text: Having many factories on River Test

parts.note: the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A town along the River Test, a Hampshire chalk stream, is full of factories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a real English river, which tempts a solver to treat 'River Test' as a single name; split it into a river and a word for test.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial area is one dominated by manufacturing plants and works.

clue.text: Aerial transport suggested for the prairies

indicators.note: something suggested is hinted at by its sound rather than spelt out

parts.note: aircraft are aerial transport

explanation.surface: Someone proposes flying as the way to cross the prairies.
explanation.definitionFit: Prairies are vast, flat grasslands, the kind of open level country also called plains.

clue.text: Surprising dim person I kept behind bars

indicators.note: a surprising version of something is unexpected, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is startled that a slow-witted person was locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be imprisoned is to be locked in jail, where the cell has bars.

clue.text: Book on trendy South Coast resort

parts.note: B is a standard abbreviation for book
right on means fashionably progressive

explanation.surface: A recommendation to reserve a stay in a fashionable seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is the abbreviation B. 'On trendy' together gives the phrase right on.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside town on the south coast of England in East Sussex.

clue.text: Reprimands favourite fellow travellers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carpet someone is to call them in for a telling-off
second meaning, whimsical: split as ..., beloved animals riding along in the vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on the carpet' is being reprimanded by a boss. The question mark flags the split into a vehicle plus pets, favourites taken on the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpets as a verb means scolds, and read as two words it describes cherished animals sharing a car ride.

clue.text: Magistrates taking native American families around UN

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the families wrap about the two-letter piece

parts.note: Native American nations are organised as tribes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Judges take on tribal groups in a case involving the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribunes were Roman officials, some with judicial powers, so the word names a kind of magistrate.

clue.text: Hatbands for mourners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: black crape bands worn on hats in mourning
second meaning: people who cry at a funeral

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea, bands worn by the bereaved, but the two nouns are separate meanings of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both those who cry and the Victorian crape bands on hats worn as a sign of grief.

clue.text: Chooses to run again arranging ad and poster

indicators.note: arranging things means placing them in a new order

parts.note: the letters of ad and poster, the joining word dropped

explanation.surface: A campaign team prepares an advert and a poster for a candidate's second bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A party that readopts a candidate selects them again to stand for election.

clue.text: St Paul's destination, travelling to China

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so they change places

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller sets out from St Paul's in London for China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Paul's' suggests the London cathedral; it is the apostle, who made Antioch the base of his missionary journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch in Syria was a city the apostle Paul repeatedly went to and set out from, as told in Acts.

clue.text: Rugby international follows a VIP eccentric to clubhouse

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters sit out of their usual order

parts.note: the letters of a VIP rearranged
a Lion plays for the British and Irish Lions rugby touring side

explanation.surface: A rugby star trails an odd celebrity on the way to the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts the rugby player after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavilion is the building at a cricket or sports ground where players change, effectively the clubhouse.

clue.text: Egyptian god from tops of ancient monument near ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins has been broken apart, so its letters are scrambled
the tops of words in a down light are their starting letters

parts.note: first letters of ancient and monument
the letters of near rearranged

explanation.surface: A god's name is traced from an old monument standing close to some ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen-Ra is the Egyptian king of the gods, a fusion of Amun and the sun god Ra.

clue.text: Foreigner needs help back into lodging

indicators.note: into means going inside, so this piece sits within the lodging

parts.note: an inn offers lodging

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end towards the start

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A visitor from abroad needs assistance getting back to their hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an Indian is a foreigner from a British viewpoint, a person from another country.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian is a national of India, so from a British setter's standpoint an example of someone from abroad.

clue.text: Pub 'Half of 21' for fictional purposes

indicators.note: half of something means only part is kept and the rest is discarded

parts.note: an inn is a pub
the answer to clue 21, the Egyptian god

explanation.surface: A pub sign reads like a riddle about some fictional purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is a cross-reference to the answer of that clue; its first three letters of six are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in name only exists nominally, as a fiction rather than in reality.

clue.text: Spin doctor live, on tour

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in arrangement

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor is out on the road, appearing live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin doctor' looks like one unit; it splits into the definition and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolution is a single complete turn about an axis, so one spin.

clue.text: Exhausted marksman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal for worn out
second meaning: someone who fires accurately

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a tired sniper, but the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot means worn out in slang, and a skilled rifleman is described as a fine shot.

clue.text: Precipitation ultimately unknown in Tamworth, perhaps?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Tamworth is a British breed of pig, and a female pig is a sow

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter is wanted

parts.note: last letter of unknown

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether it never snows in the Staffordshire town of Tamworth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town but also a ginger pig breed named after it; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen water falling from clouds, one form of precipitation alongside rain and hail.

clue.text: Stop dead and liberate heartless zombie

parts.note: to free is to liberate

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its interior and keeps only its ends

parts.note: outer letters of zombie

explanation.surface: A horror-film hero halts, then releases a zombie with no heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to become suddenly motionless, as when startled.

clue.text: Contents from small Red strongholds

parts.note: Com. is the short form of Communist, a Red
forts are strongholds

explanation.surface: Something taken from minor Communist bases is listed as their contents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents' looks like a noun meaning what is inside; it is the verb, as in contents a child. 'small' signals the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to soothe and satisfy them, which is what contents means as a verb.
